sampling_model.design: Independent sampling from a two-arm trial; the probabilities \(\pi_a(X)\) are known protocol-fixed design inputs and are not conditions defining either compatible-law class.
sampling_model.units: Each unit has finite genomic profile \(Z\), a predeclared continuous score \(R\), bounded potential event times, and potential censoring times.
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment \(A\in\{0,1\}\) is independent of \((T(0),T(1),C(0),C(1))\) conditional on \(X=(Z,R)\).
sampling_model.overlap: The lower bounds \(\pi_a(x)\ge\varepsilon\) hold for both treatment arms, and uncensored probability is bounded below by \(\kappa\). Because treatment is binary and the two allocation probabilities sum to one, \(\pi_a(x)\le1-\varepsilon\) is a consequence rather than a separate overlap restriction.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The bounded score-density and known-\(\beta\) Hölder conditions are explicit maintained regularity restrictions. No nuisance-band theorem is inferred from them. Inference is stated only over the externally certified subclass \(\mathfrak P_n^{\mathrm{band}}(r_n)\), with abstract radius \(r_n\), and the empirical-process prerequisite is imposed only on \(\mathcal D_n\times\mathcal G_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 5.1 bounds each covariatewise CATE by differencing armwise conservative CAPO endpoints under the causal conditions in Assumption 3.1.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The Wang-compatible box-sharpness theorem and the exact obstacle-strictness theorem

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper characterizes sharp response-function regions under selective observation and shape restrictions using random-set capacity and Aumann-expectation methods.
Theorem 1 gives sharp DTE bounds under support restrictions by optimal-transport duality.
Theorem 1 computes projections of a shape-restricted sieve confidence region by two linear programs.
Theorems 3.2 and 4.1 derive directional limits for uniform functionals of optimized value maps with a fixed feasible correspondence.
The paper diagnoses ordinary-bootstrap failure for nonlinear directional derivatives and validates derivative-aware resampling.
Theorem 3.1 gives a uniform Gaussian support-function process for set-identified linear models using orthogonal moments and sample splitting.
Theorem 1 gives efficient joint Gaussian inference for a supplied family of point-identified subgroup effects.
The paper constructs winner's-curse-adjusted inference for a selected approximately Gaussian scalar target.

body.tldr: Informative dropout leaves an unknown residual restricted-survival contribution along the predeclared prognostic score. The greatest feasible monotone \(L\)-Lipschitz residual below a capacity \(u\) is the explicit envelope \(\Gamma_Lu\), which gives the exact pointwise projection of the law-sharp compact CATE-curve set. Joint curve coupling is nontrivial: the maintained set is strictly smaller than the Wang endpoint-selection box exactly when some arm-profile dropout capacity is nonzero. Support values separate into certified path-flow obstacle programs, and eroded grids have a uniform Hausdorff remainder even at zero-capacity contacts. For inference, a direct positive-part stability argument turns an externally certified nuisance band into an observable clipped compact convex whole-set superset with directed excess \(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), without face differentiation or a direction net. Combining the density band with a finite-multinomial profile-mass region gives conservative simultaneous intervals for every eligible leaf and arbitrary post-selection validity. Efficient local-mass \((np_{\min,n})^{-1/2}\) calibration remains open because the declared score assumptions contain no score-to-statistic expansion or multiplier coupling.

project_justification.gap: Wang et al. prove covariatewise outer endpoint validity under their treatment-exchangeability, overlap, and consistency conditions, but do not characterize the jointly attainable curve image, its exact contraction under score-shape restrictions, or an estimated-obstacle confidence set that remains valid when capacity contacts change. Generic support-function and directional-bootstrap results do not supply the missing score-to-statistic expansion for the present obstacle program.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is simultaneously causal and functional: a law-sharp compact set of whole CATE curves, an exact published-class benchmark modulo \(P_X\)-null sets, a finite flow certificate, and an observable confidence superset whose validity does not depend on stable active faces.
project_justification.fill: Completion witnesses establish exact population identification in the monotone-Lipschitz class and transfer converse attainability from the continuous witness subclass to the full Wang-compatible class. The envelope, strictness, support-flow, grid-Hausdorff, and stability results characterize and compute the population set. On the externally certified band-valid subclass, the proved band-robust theorem establishes uniform containment of the true curve set in the robust union together with shrinking directed excess; a finite-multinomial baseline-law region yields conservative simultaneous leaf projections with the theorem's stated outer-probability guarantee. Only the sharper derivative-aware local-mass multiplier rate is left unresolved.

body.related_work: Wang et al. (2025, Assumption 3.1, Theorem 5.1, equations (8)--(9), and Appendix D.2) provide treatment-exchangeability, overlap, consistency, and conservative arm and CATE endpoint results. This note first states their compatible-law class explicitly, proves their endpoint-selection box is the full measurable image modulo \(P_X\)-null sets by transferring completion witnesses from a smaller continuous subclass, and then shows that its continuous slice is \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\). The maintained monotone-Lipschitz model is a distinct sensitivity class: its greatest-obstacle envelope gives exact pointwise projections, and its joint curve image is strictly smaller than the Wang box if and only if at least one capacity is nonzero. Beresteanu, Molchanov, and Molinari inform the support-function view of set identification; Kim informs primal--dual certification; and Chiang et al. inform finite linear encodings of shape restrictions. None supplies the informative-dropout completion or the exact obstacle envelope proved here. Firpo, Galvao, and Parker, Fang and Santos, and Semenova motivate derivative-aware inference for optimized maps, but their results do not create a score-to-statistic expansion for an estimated infinite-dimensional obstacle with changing contacts. The present whole-set theorem instead uses a direct Hausdorff contraction and an external nuisance band, so it needs neither face differentiation nor a direction net. Wei et al. motivate simultaneous subgroup inference for a supplied family of point-identified effects; here density-band and finite-multinomial uncertainty are propagated through a partially identified curve set to give conservative simultaneous and post-selection leaf intervals. The efficient local-mass multiplier refinement remains a separate open problem.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The completion uses the convention \(\Delta=\mathbf 1\{C\le T\}\), so assigning \(T=C\) to the non-maximal branch remains recorded as dropout. If a data system codes ties as observed events, exact attainment at zero residual may fail and the sharp object can become a closure; that alternative convention must be audited before application.
body.honest_scope: Population claims are exact but class-specific. The maintained monotone-Lipschitz compatible-law class has the law-sharp curve set and exact \(\Gamma_Lu\) pointwise projection; the full Wang-compatible class has the measurable endpoint-selection box modulo \(P_X\)-null sets, with \(\mathcal B(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\) as its continuous slice. The finite-\(L\) and monotonicity restrictions are novel identifying sensitivities, while score density and known-\(\beta\) Hölder regularity are explicit regularity conditions. No nuisance band is derived from those conditions: inference is uniform only over the externally certified subclass. On the band event, the proved whole-set superset covers and has directed excess at most \(8r_n+2(Lh_n+Mh_n^\beta)\), uniformly through changing contacts. Conservative leaf intervals additionally use a finite-multinomial profile-mass region; their displayed excess shrinks under \((r_n+n^{-1/2})/p_{\min,n}\to0\), which is stronger than the desired local-mass regime. The current envelope, moment, and entropy assumptions do not imply a statistic expansion or conditional multiplier approximation, so no efficient \((np_{\min,n})^{-1/2}\) leaf claim is made. Post-selection validity is deterministic on the simultaneous event. An ADJUVANT sign reanalysis still requires individual trial records, a genuinely predeclared score, eligible leaf mass, and a defensible sensitivity value \(L\); absent those inputs, no empirical subgroup sign is asserted.
